scope: Daily NASA FIRMS active-fire detections over the North China Plain, reduced to regional and upwind counts for a central-Beijing receptor. Produced by scripts/ingest/fetch_firms.py.

files.Beijing_fire_firms.csv: One row per day: detections and total FRP within 300 km, plus the subset lying upwind of Beijing given that day's mean wind direction.

sources.authority: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System), LANCE/ESDIS
sources.title: VIIRS S-NPP 375 m Active Fire product, standard-processing archive (VIIRS_SNPP_SP)
sources.notes: Archive (SP) product, available from 2012-01-20; the NRT feeds hold only recent months. Search region west,south,east,north = 114,37,119,41. The API caps a request at a 5-day window but has no job queue.

sources.title: datasets/Beijing.csv hourly wind direction
sources.notes: Daily mean wind direction is the circular (unit-vector) mean of the hourly wd compass values across all stations, mapped N=0 ... NNW=337.5.

extraction.upwind_definition: A detection is upwind when the great-circle bearing from the receptor to the fire lies within +/-45 degrees of wind_from_deg, the direction the wind blows FROM.
extraction.deduplication: Detections are de-duplicated on (latitude, longitude, acq_date, acq_time) because repeated or overlapping 5-day pulls can return the same record.
extraction.coverage_range: 2013-03-01 .. 2017-03-04 (the tail extends a few days past the benchmark record because the API window is a fixed 5 days)

known_limitations: These are satellite DETECTIONS, not emissions. Fire radiative power is an observed radiance quantity; converting it to pollutant emissions requires emission factors that are not applied here.

Detection is strongly cloud-limited. Measured over June 2014, detections correlate POSITIVELY with the temperature-dewpoint gap (r = +0.37, i.e. clear dry days) while PM2.5 correlates NEGATIVELY with it (r = -0.53). Detected fire counts therefore anti-correlate with pollution, and any attribution built on raw counts is confounded by detection bias rather than measuring a causal effect.
Small or short-lived fires below the 375 m detection threshold are missed, and overpass timing means sub-daily burning is sampled, not integrated.
wind_from_deg is a single city-wide daily mean; it cannot represent wind shifts within a day or spatial variation of the flow across a 300 km source region.
The 300 km radius and +/-45 degree sector are analysis choices, not physical constants; transport distance depends on wind speed and lifetime.

Absence of a date row means no FIRMS detection within the receptor radius that day. This is USUALLY zero fires, but can also be a cloud-obscured or no-overpass miss — a missing row is not an asserted zero. Whether to treat missing days as zero in a continuity or daily-mean analysis is the analyst's call, not a claim of the data; the rows are not gap-filled.
